result:
If I could change the world in one way, I would rewire human motivation so that the drive to build accurate models of reality became as automatic and satisfying as food or sex. 

Right now, most behavior orbits around status, belonging, immediate comfort, and narrative comfort. These instincts made sense for small tribes on the savanna, but they scale poorly to a planet with nuclear weapons, global markets, and AI systems. The result is a species that routinely chooses comforting stories over evidence, short-term wins over compounding progress, and tribal loyalty over figuring out how things actually work.

That single adjustment would not magically solve every problem. It would still leave room for disagreement, error, and conflict. But it would tilt the entire distribution of decisions toward better calibration with physical reality instead of against it. Science would advance faster because fewer people would treat it as optional. Institutions would face real pressure to update when data contradicted them. Individuals would spend less time optimizing for applause and more time optimizing for understanding.

Everything else—poverty reduction, risk mitigation, even the quality of art and humor—tends to follow from clearer thinking about cause and effect. The universe does not care about our preferences, but it does respond consistently to accurate maps of itself. Giving humans a stronger instinct for those maps seems like the highest-leverage edit.
